(AP) — President Donald Trump is emphasizing his influence during his second term at a rally in Kentucky. He claimed on Saturday that he could achieve "unbelievable" things, citing his decision to change how the U.S. government refers to the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. Trump was in Highland Heights to support Republican candidates, including Ed Gallrein for the U.S. House. Trump warned that a Democratic win could reverse his policies. Vance faces tough questions on Iran war, immigration and more in CBS town hall WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — Vice President JD Vance faced tough questions from voters about the Trump administration’s policies on data centers, high costs, immigration and his own rhetoric in a town hall on CBS News that aired Saturday night. The string of sharp queries, some from voters who said they had supported him and President Donald Trump, previewed the rocky path he may face trying to answer for the administration’s record if he runs for president himself. Major fire breaks out in Alberta after deadly incident at Canadian military base EDMONTON, Alberta (AP) — Canada’s defense minister says that people have been killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire, while reports said that large numbers of injured people were being transported to hospitals. Fire crews scrambled late into the night Saturday as fierce winds whipped flames beyond Canadian Forces Base Wainwright and into the surrounding rural area. It was not immediately clear how many people were killed or injured, but a doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, 120 miles northwest, told Canada’s national broadcaster that patients were being brought to hospitals across the city as health-care facilities around the base became “completely overwhelmed” by the number of people needing care. Blaze at St Petersburg oil sites as Kyiv launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia Ukrainian attacks have set an oil export terminal ablaze in St. Petersburg. Kyiv launched over 1,000 drones across Russia in one of its largest aerial bombardments. The attack comes amid tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. One person was killed and five were wounded in the attack, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city’s Ruchi oil depot. Meanwhile, one woman died and at least two other people were injured after Russia launched two attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said. Pope returns to Vatican days after surgery; surgeon says he should be fit for Latin America tour VATICAN CITY (AP) — The surgeon who removed Pope Leo XIV's cancerous tumor says there are “no clinical reasons” to prevent the pontiff from traveling to Latin America next month. Vatican media reported this after the pope returned to the Vatican from the hospital. Dr. Stefano Margaritora told Vatican News that the pope is expected to recover fully from surgery in about 10 days. Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. He left the hospital on Saturday, well ahead of the week-long hospital stay the Vatican had initially anticipated. Trump's decision to waive Russian sanctions outrages Congress, but no quick counter seen WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump’s abrupt decision to waive sanctions on Russia is drawing outrage and concern from members of Congress. Trump's move came late Friday, two days before the penalties were scheduled to take effect. Republican Sen. Thom Tillis says Trump's move is “beyond irresponsible.” Lawmakers had overwhelmingly passed the legislation in a bipartisan display of U.S. support for Ukraine. Trump signed it into law last month. The waiver is the latest instance of Trump drawing the U.S. closer to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump recently announced a diesel deal with Putin to import Russian energy in hopes of curbing high gas prices in the U.S. that are roiling the midterm elections. Masked settlers attack European diplomats in the occupied West Bank JERUSALEM (AP) — Masked settlers attacked a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank, a French mayor who was struck and others say. The attackers targeted Belgium’s consul general and French and Polish diplomats on Saturday, Belgium's foreign minister said. The French mayor described the attack by men with metal bars. Israel’s military condemned the attack as a “severe act of violence,” and police said they had opened an investigation. But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned against “premature conclusions.” At least four people have been killed since the olive harvest began in the Palestinian territory earlier this month, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. Oregon father is the latest armed civilian to confront a gunman in a US mass shooting Few mass shootings in the U.S. end with an armed civilian confronting the gunman, as happened during the deadly attack on an Oregon elementary school. Kenda Freeman said her son, Kaylub Giamanco, intervened by firing his own weapon after the shooting began at his daughters’ school in the town of Bend. President Donald Trump and others praised Giamanco, but such interventions remain rare. Gun rights advocates argue the “good guy with a gun” is needed for public safety. Gun control advocates have argued that a civilian with a gun could confuse responding police or cause more harm in a chaotic situation. Search continues after boat capsizes off Baja California coast. Survivors attacked by sharks The U.S. Coast Guard reports that multiple survivors have been treated for suspected shark bites after a boat capsized off Baja California. The boat, which departed from Mexico, was carrying 27 people. Sixteen Mexican nationals were rescued on Friday, but authorities continue searching for 11 missing individuals. The Coast Guard and Navy are using aircraft and boats, with help from the Mexican Navy. The boat capsized in waters frequented by smugglers. The Mexican consulate in San Diego confirmed all rescued were Mexican nationals. Customs and Border Protection is investigating, and efforts to locate the missing continue. items.excerpt: Retail price impacts from the Iran war are uneven but add up for US households before midterms NEW YORK (AP) — High fuel prices are making it more expensive to drive, fly and buy some goods more than seven months into the U.S.-Iran war. That's prolonging the strain on American households as the midterm elections approach., The chief economist at Moody’s Analytics estimates the war has cost the average U.S. household the equivalent of almost $2,000, including $1,100 related to energy. Motorists and airline passengers so far have borne the clearest consequences from disrupted Middle East oil shipments. The elevated cost of making and moving goods hasn't translated into across-the-board retail price increases. Shoppers may not be spared indefinitely, though. U.S. consumers are uneasy about the increasingly high-tech ways that restaurant chains and major retailers are setting prices. Digital price tags are replacing paper ones in grocery aisles. Artificial intelligence tools help businesses decide what to charge by predicting how customers might respond. Terms like “dynamic pricing” and “surveillance pricing” are stirring up anger and anxiety on social media. Much of the concern focuses on whether customer data is getting used to give different people different prices for the same product. Walmart and McDonald's say critics misunderstand how their pricing tools work. Lawmakers and regulators are taking preemptive action to restrict when companies can use personal data in pricing. BANGKOK (AP) — U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says he won't prejudge what the U.S. central bank will do about interest rates at its upcoming meetings. However, he repeatedly vowed to “deliver price stability.” Warsh spoke Friday on the sidelines of a meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok. The global surge in prices is a key concern of the financial leaders meeting. Stubbornly high U.S. inflation is expected to lead the Fed to raise its key interest rate in coming months after a rate hike in September.

items.title: Inflation Shakes Fed Outlook Crude Oil Surges, Sanders Targets Oil Companies and More: This Week in Economy
items.excerpt: My Account Benzinga Premium Premium Services All sections October 18, 2026 6:00 AM2 min read # Inflation Shakes Fed Outlook Crude Oil Surges, Sanders Targets Oil Companies and More: This Week in Economy Markets faced a sharp change in tone as inflation data challenged Fed expectations and energy costs kept pressure on households. Here are five stories that shaped the weekend conversation. ## Hotter Inflation Shakes Up The Fed Outlook A hotter-than-expected September consumer price index disrupted expectations for the Federal Reserve’s October meeting, which had looked set for a hold. The data lifted expectations for an October rate increase and revived concerns about currency debasement and persistent price pressures. Read the full article here. ## Brent Crude Hits $110 As Wars Disrupt Oil Supplies Brent crude hit $110 per barrel on Friday, its highest level since May 20, and closed at $109.86 as the U.S.-Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars keep disrupting global energy supplies. Regular gasoline averaged about $4.33 per gallon and diesel $6.32, nearly $2.67 higher than a year ago. Read the full article here. ## Vance Points To Wartime Authority For Texas Refinery Expansion Vice President JD Vance said the Trump administration plans to use wartime authority to expand fuel production at Delek US Holdings Inc. (NYSE: DK)’s refinery in Tyler, Texas. The move comes as higher gas prices strain household budgets weeks before the midterms. Read the full article here. ## Sanders Targets Oil Companies With A Windfall-Tax Proposal Sen.\*\* Bernie Sanders\*\* (I-Vt.) called for a windfall profits tax on oil companies after President Donald Trump said the U.S. was benefiting from high oil prices linked to the Iran war. "America is not making ‘a fortune’ off high gas prices, but your Big Oil pals are," Sanders wrote on X. Read the full article here. ## 5. Chamath Palihapitiya Warns Of A Bond-Yield Shock Venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya said a 10-year Treasury yield of 5.5% to 6% could "run over" businesses dependent on financing spreads, including AI companies. He said the concern is not specific to AI but tied to debt-to-GDP ratios and pressures across Western economies. Read the full article here. Lawmakers from both parties blasted the executive order late Friday, the latest in a series of steps that the Republican president has taken drawing the United States closer to Russia's Vladimir Putin. Trump recently announced a diesel deal with Putin to import Russian energy in a long-shot effort to curb high gas prices in the U.S. that are roiling the midterm elections on Nov. 3.

items.title: Tini: FUTTURA World Tour | Miami & Miami Beach
items.excerpt: # Tini: FUTTURA World Tour ### Oct 18, 2026 ##### Doors open: 7:00 PM | Show starts: 8:00 PM ... Argentine pop artist Tini brings her FUTTURA World Tour to downtown Miami for the tour’s only U.S. stop. Tini: FUTTURA World Tour takes place Sunday, October 18, 2026 at Kaseya Center. The tour is described as a retrospective project spanning Tini’s different musical eras, from her early international breakthrough on Disney Channel Latin America’s Violetta to her solo career in pop, urbano, cumbia and alternative pop. The Miami concert follows the tour’s launch in Buenos Aires and brings the arena production to a U.S. audience for one night only. Born Martina Stoessel, Tini is an Argentine singer, actress and performer whose albums include Tini, Quiero Volver, Tini Tini Tini, Cupido and Un Mechón de Pelo. Her career includes chart success in Latin America and Europe, multiple major music awards and collaborations that have expanded her reach across Latin pop and global music audiences. The event is open to all ages, though ages 18 and older are recommended.
